item.title: Chinese giant panda pair meets public at Zoo Atlanta
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
ATLANTA, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- Crisp autumn air hovered over Atlanta as giant panda Ping Ping sat peacefully in the outdoor yard, lazily munching on bamboo stalks, while indoors, Fu Shuang reposed lazily atop a wooden climbing structure. Following a month-long quarantine, the pair of six-year-old giant pandas officially stepped into the spotlight at Zoo Atlanta on Friday, welcoming a crowd of eager onlookers. Images of "Ping Ping" and "Fu Shuang" are displayed above the zoo's entrance gate. Lamp posts from the entrance to the Panda Grove hang posters reading "Meet Ping Ping", "Meet Fu Shuang" and "New Pandas, New Habitat." The all-new Panda Grove has two rooms and two outdoor habitats. This is where the pandas will stay for the next 10 years, according to an agreement between Zoo Atlanta and the China Wildlife Conservation Association. The zoo held a grand ceremony to mark the pair's debut. Addressing the ceremony, Zoo Atlanta President and CEO Raymond King hailed the return of pandas as "a historic moment for Zoo Atlanta." "As we welcome Ping Ping and Fu Shuang to our city, we also celebrate the power of partnership ... This extraordinary spirit of partnership helps create a future for a species that is truly beloved the world over," King said. "The arrival of the new pair of pandas is China's sincere response to the aspirations of the American people," said Xie Feng, Chinese Ambassador to the United States, in his speech at the ceremony. "It is your enthusiasm and dedication that have turned people's dreams into reality and brought pandas across the Pacific for a joyful gathering," Xie said, depicting the pandas' arrival as a vivid testament to the practical subnational cooperation between China and the United States. "This has not only forged more bonds of affinity between our two peoples, but also contributed a joint China-U.S. solution to global biodiversity protection, and thus served as a compelling example of how China and the United States, working together, can get a lot of big and great things done," he said. U.S. Ambassador to China David Perdue, City of Atlanta Mayor Andre Dickens and State of Georgia Governor and First Lady Brian and Marty Kemp sent welcome messages via video. Fifteen minutes after the zoo opened, the line of visitors zigzagged outside the grove. Children screamed with excitement at the sight of Ping Ping outdoors, while taking pictures and selfies with the giant pandas became a must-do for visitors. Amanda and her husband brought their 8-year-old son and 3-year-old daughter here to meet Ping Ping and Fu Shuang. "I was his age when Zoo Atlanta got their pandas the first time, so I felt like it was really important to bring them here to kind of relive that experience myself and for them to have it too," she told Xinhua. Debi Nicholson came all the way from Florida to see the pandas. "I am ecstatic. They're beautiful," she said. "I just hope they live forever." "The keepers that will take care of Ping Ping and Fu Shuang took care of the previous pair of pandas," King told Xinhua in an interview. "Our first and foremost priority in the near future is making sure they're comfortably adjusted." "Pandamonium is real. People are lined up at the gates," King said. "I would imagine that our attendance will grow between 10 and 20 percent in the first year just from having pandas. It drives panda merchandise. It drives panda gifts and cups ... It certainly has a big economic impact on the zoo." ■

item.description:

This photo taken on Nov. 7, 2026 shows a scene of the opening ceremony of the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing, capital of China. The summit kicked off here on Saturday. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) BEIJING, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- The 7th World Media Summit held its opening ceremony in Beijing on Saturday under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action." Xinhua News Agency and the Beijing municipal government jointly organized this year's summit, which runs from Thursday to Monday. It drew nearly 500 representatives from nearly 330 mainstream media outlets, think tanks and government bodies from 112 countries and regions, as well as the United Nations and other international organizations. Li Shulei, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony. The World Media Summit was initiated in 2009 and is now a major global platform for media exchange and cooperation. The last summit was held in Urumqi, the capital city of northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, in 2024. ■ This photo taken on Nov. 7, 2026 shows a scene of the opening ceremony of the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing, capital of China. item.title: China successfully launches CERES-2 carrier rocket
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
A CERES-2 Y3 carrier rocket with four satellites onboard blasts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 7, 2026. The rocket blasted off at 7:37 a.m. (Beijing Time) and successfully sent the satellites into the planned orbit. (Photo by Wang Jiangbo/Xinhua) JIUQUAN, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- China on Saturday launched a CERES-2 Y3 carrier rocket with four satellites onboard. The rocket blasted off at 7:37 a.m. (Beijing Time) from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China and successfully sent the satellites into a 535-km sun-synchronous orbit. The four satellites belong to different fields, ranging from ocean remote sensing and commercial meteorology to university-led scientific research and space situational awareness. The rocket development team said the successful flight test and the precise orbital insertion of the four satellites mark the official entry into service of a new commercial launch vehicle. The CERES-2 is a medium-lift launch vehicle developed for the commercial launch market. As an upgraded model in the CERES series, it features a configuration of three tandem solid stages plus a liquid upper stage. With a liftoff mass of about 100 tonnes, it can deliver a payload of 1.3 tonnes to a 500-km sun-synchronous orbit and is capable of both land and sea launches. A representative from the rocket's developer, Galactic Energy, said the company will continue to focus on improving the efficiency and reliability of its solid launch vehicles, helping meet China's multi-tiered launch needs for small and medium satellite constellation deployment, replenishment, and the build-out of medium-to-large constellations. ■ A CERES-2 Y3 carrier rocket with four satellites onboard blasts off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China, Nov. 7, 2026. item.title: First foreign astronaut to board Chinese space station
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
BEIJING, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- A Pakistani astronaut will join the Shenzhou-24 crewed flight mission as a payload specialist, the China Manned Space Agency said on Saturday. After completing a short on-orbit flight, the Pakistani astronaut will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft. With China's space station going to receive the first foreign visitor, the mission will mark the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of the country's manned space program. In February 2025, China and Pakistan signed a cooperation agreement on astronaut selection, training and participation in Chinese space station flight missions in Islamabad, officially launching astronaut selection from Pakistan. After a rigorous three-stage selection and assessment process, two Pakistani reserve astronauts were selected. After completing all training and passing the evaluation in China, one will carry out the crewed flight mission while the other will serve as a backup. ■

item.title: Int'l seminar explores CPC's self-governance practices, global implications
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
Qu Qingshan, president of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, addresses an international seminar on understanding the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Cai Yang) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- An international seminar on understanding the recently concluded key Communist Party of China (CPC) plenum was held in Beijing on Friday, bringing together more than 200 diplomats, think tank experts and media representatives from 105 countries and international organizations. At the seminar, a report titled "Putting the People First -- Values Underpinning Full and Rigorous Self-Governance of the CPC" was jointly released by the national high-level think tanks of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee and Xinhua News Agency. EXPOUNDING ON THE PLENUM The seminar focused on the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, with participants discussing the CPC's achievements and the significance of full and rigorous Party self-governance, governance through institutions and rules, and principle of putting the people first. In his address, Qu Qingshan, president of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, said the plenary session was a highly important meeting held at a crucial stage in China's efforts to basically achieve socialist modernization. The session made strategic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, fully demonstrating the CPC Central Committee's strong sense of historical initiative in strengthening the Party and the country, Qu said. Fu Hua, president of Xinhua News Agency, said that guided by the Resolution of the Central Committee of the CPC on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance, adopted at the plenum, the CPC will continue to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance from a new historical starting point, further strengthening its capacity to govern and its leadership capabilities. Fu also said that Xinhua stands ready to work with all parties to deepen systematic and theoretical research and interpretation of major issues concerning Party building in the new era and help the international community better understand China and the CPC. Lyu Yansong, Xinhua's editor-in-chief, said that as China strives to build a great modern socialist country and achieve its second centenary goal, sustained efforts to strengthen Party self-governance are essential to ensuring that the CPC remains a strong leadership core in the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The resolution adopts a systematic approach, with its various measures designed to reinforce one another in terms of objectives, implementation and outcomes, ensuring that the Party's governance practices keep pace with the times, follow established principles and embrace innovation, said Huang Yibing, vice president of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee. SHARING INSIGHTS ON GLOBAL SIGNIFICANCE International participants shared their perspectives on the CPC's governance practices and their implications for political parties around the world. Zafar Uddin Mahmood, special representative of the prime minister of Pakistan on China affairs, said China's governance model and its ability to maintain institutional continuity, implement long-term plans and respond to new challenges have attracted widespread international attention. Patricio Giusto, executive director of the Observatory of Argentina-China Relations, said the CPC had offered an effective and resolute response to corruption from within -- one of the oldest challenges associated with political power. The CPC has built its political practice on strict discipline, stable institutional norms and sound intra-Party regulations, he said, adding that keeping power within the bounds of institutions is one of the key pillars of its success in Party governance. Josef Gregory Mahoney, a professor of politics and international relations at East China Normal University, said the CPC had long recognized that unchecked corruption and pointless formalities could erode public trust and undermine its governing capacity. The CPC regards improving intra-Party regulations as a long-term and fundamental approach to advancing full and rigorous self-governance, a practice worthy of study by political parties in other countries, he said. item.title: Xiplomacy: Xi's reply inspires Australian students to carry forward friendship
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
ADELAIDE, Australia, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- As spring unfolds in the Southern Hemisphere, a message of friendship has crossed the ocean. Chinese President Xi Jinping recently replied to 110 young Australian students who had written to him, encouraging them to remain committed to promoting the China-Australia friendship. In his letter dated Oct. 28, Xi said he was pleased to learn that the students recently visited China to take part in the Sino-Australian Collegiate Rowing and Dragon Boat Friendship Challenge, where they competed alongside Chinese university students, engaged in in-depth exchanges, forged friendships that transcended borders, and created wonderful memories together. For many of the young Australians, the visit was more than a sporting and cultural exchange. It offered an opportunity to see China firsthand, connect with their Chinese peers and gain a deeper appreciation of the country. Xi's reply has given their experience added significance, resonating with both the students and education professionals who helped make the exchange possible. In July 2025, Xi met with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese in Beijing. Stressing the importance of cultivating people-to-people ties, Xi said Australians from all walks of life are welcome to visit the country and China stands ready to invite more Australian youth for exchange programs. The invitation was taken up in September, when more than 100 students and staff members from six leading Australian universities, including the University of Sydney, Adelaide University and the University of New South Wales, visited China. In China's eastern city of Nanjing, the young Australians joined students from Chinese universities, including Nanjing University and Tongji University, for the rowing and dragon boat event. Beyond the competition, the event also offered participants a chance to appreciate China's traditional dragon boat culture. The connections made during the trip did not end when the students returned home. After their trip to China, the students jointly wrote a letter to Xi and Albanese, sharing their experiences during their visit, expressing admiration for China's long-lasting history and rich culture, as well as its scientific and technological innovation capabilities. They also voiced their eagerness to help carry forward the bilateral friendship and foster greater mutual understanding. On Friday, Xi's reply was presented to representatives of the young Australians in Adelaide, South Australia's capital. For Daniel Wiersema, a student representative from Adelaide University, receiving the letter was a particularly moving moment. Recalling the visit to China, he expressed gratitude to Xi for the opportunity and the experience. "We want to thank him, and hope that our countries can become really, really good friends in the future," he said. Jason Slater, head of Sport Development at Adelaide University Sport and Fitness, said he had spoken with students from all the participating Australian universities and found that they indeed enjoyed the trip. The letter to the two leaders brought together the students' individual experiences and reflections, conveying personal stories and a strong sense of friendship, he said. Xi's reply was "very important encouragement," Slater said. Many participants now hoped to return to China for further studies and explore opportunities to build connections with the country in their future careers, he said. Elise Courtney, a student at the University of New South Wales, recalled her excitement at receiving Xi's reply. "We know how busy it must be for him to take the time to reply to us. It was really special," she said. She also showed Xinhua a team jersey she had swapped with a Chinese teammate, describing it as a treasured keepsake of the trip. In their letter, the students recalled seeing China's dynamic, modern cities while also experiencing its rich history and cultural heritage. The contrast and combination left a strong impression on them. Beyond the individual memories, the exchange also brought home a broader message about the role of young people in shaping bilateral relations. China and Australia share a longstanding tradition of friendly exchanges, Xi noted in the letter, adding that the future of bilateral relations lies with the younger generation. He voiced hope that the Australian students can continue to actively contribute to the cause of friendship between the two countries, serve as torchbearers of the friendship and cooperation between the two countries, and carry forward this friendship from generation to generation. For Anja Felderhof, a student from Adelaide University, that message struck a particular chord. "That was my take-away sentence," she said. "All of my friends in Australia can say we're pretty excited to continue this friendship as well," she added. The importance of such exchanges extends beyond the students themselves, offering universities an opportunity to build lasting institutional links. Rongyu Li, deputy vice-chancellor and vice-president (global engagement) of the University of Queensland, told Xinhua that face-to-face exchanges among young people from the two countries can deepen mutual understanding and foster friendship. He said Xi's reply would encourage more Australian universities to actively participate in exchanges and further strengthen cooperation with China.■

item.title: CPC initiates election process for delegates to 21st national congress
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
BEIJING, Nov. 7 (Xinhua) -- The Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (CPC) has released a circular for the election of delegates to the Party's 21st national congress, making comprehensive plans for related work. The Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee has made detailed arrangements for the election, according to an official statement released Saturday. The CPC will convene its 21st national congress in the second half of 2027 in Beijing, the 20th CPC Central Committee decided at its fifth plenary session in late October. The congress comes at a critical time when the CPC has been working to basically realize socialist modernization and heading toward the Second Centenary Goal. It will be a highly important meeting and an event of great political significance for both the Party and the country, the statement said. The election of the delegates will lay an important foundation for the success of this congress, it said. Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, convened meetings of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee to study the matter in depth and set out overall requirements, objectives and tasks for carrying out the work, according to the statement. A total of 2,360 delegates to the congress will be elected by 38 electoral units across the country, the statement said. It urged putting political standards first, applying strict eligibility criteria, following rigorous electoral procedures, and strictly enforcing electoral discipline, to ensure that those elected are of high caliber, well-structured in composition, and broadly representative, with the support of Party members. The statement stressed the importance of examining candidates' political stance and awareness, as well as their capacity for political judgment, thinking and implementation. It also called for strict scrutiny of candidates' integrity and conduct. Front-line workers should account for an appropriate proportion of the delegates. Efforts must be made to recommend model workers, farmers and professionals as candidates in the election. Women Party members and Party members from ethnic minority groups should each make up a certain proportion of the delegates. The delegates should come from a wide range of fields, including the economy, science and technology, national defense, law enforcement and the justice system, education, public communication, culture, health, sports and social administration. The delegates should also include workers in new forms of employment, the statement said. The delegates will be elected through a process in which the number of candidates must exceed the number of seats by more than 15 percent. The statement stressed the need to ensure oversight throughout the electoral process and maintain zero tolerance for violations of rules, discipline and laws. Any violation should be resolutely investigated and dealt with, it added. It urged making the election a process of studying and implementing Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, particularly Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building. The election will run from now until the end of June 2027. ■

item.title: China, Gabon elevate ties to community with shared future for new era
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema in Beijing on Friday. The two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. Noting China is willing to be a reliable friend and partner for Gabon in its independent development, Xi said China supports Gabon in maintaining independence in political, economic and diplomatic affairs, and will join hands with Gabon to build a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. Xi said China is ready to work with Gabon to maintain close communication at all levels, exchange experience in political party and state governance, and support Gabon in strengthening its governance capacity. Hailing the strong economic complementarity and great potential for cooperation between the two countries, Xi called on both sides to strengthen the alignment of their development strategies and cultivate new growth drivers for cooperation. He called for making good use of the new opportunities presented by zero-tariff treatment of African goods and the "green channel" facilitation measures for African agricultural and food products exported to China. Both sides should expand and upgrade bilateral trade and investment cooperation to support Gabon's industrial development, job creation, and livelihood improvement, thereby enhancing the country's capacity for independent economic development, Xi said. "The vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity and the four major global initiatives I have proposed serve, first and foremost, the common interests of the Global South and African countries," Xi said, adding that China supports Gabon in playing a greater role in international and regional affairs. Nguema said Gabon firmly adheres to the one-China principle, and hopes to draw on China's successful experience in governance of party and country. He said Gabon stands ready to further deepen practical cooperation with China, and welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in Gabon to help Gabon achieve industrialization and sustainable development. Noting that China has established a mutually beneficial and win-win partnership with Africa, Nguema said the zero-tariff policy meets the needs of African countries, enabling African products to enter the vast Chinese market, which is of historic significance to the development of African countries. He added Gabon is willing to work with China to enhance solidarity and cooperation between Africa and China and jointly safeguard the interests of Global South countries. After the talks, the two heads of state witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering the implementation of the Global Security Initiative, zero-tariff treatment, industrial and supply chains, Chinese language education, and other fields. During Nguema's state visit to China, the two sides issued a joint statement on building a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Nguema in the Great Hall of the People. Xi also held a welcome banquet for him in the evening. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping holds a welcome ceremony for Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema in the Northern Hall of the Great Hall of the People prior to their talks in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, casts his ballot to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses. ■ Chinese Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Ziguangge polling station of the Wenjin Street electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026.
